paper.purpose: The ground the application is printed on: body, sheet interiors, input fields, the unfilled part of every band.

paper-2.purpose: Zebra table row, index-column ground, disabled control, empty-state field, chart-head identification cell.

paper-3.purpose: Section heads and sticky table header cells — the tint a form uses for the part printed before anyone wrote on it.

rule.purpose: The lightest rule: row dividers, band track borders, the 8px chart grid.

rule-2.purpose: The structural rule: sheet outline, section head, table head, input box, and the 3px double rule.

ink.purpose: Every primary word, the masthead mark's border, the live reference detent, the modal scrim at 60%.

ink-2.purpose: Secondary text, field labels, annotations, unmeasured figures, the hatch stroke at 20%, the ghost detent, the scrollbar thumb.

chart.purpose: The single structural accent — links, the filled primary button, the inked active nav item, the focus outline, the 7%/12% row washes, selection at 22%, accent-color and caret-color. Also the `info` status ink.

band.purpose: Status ink `ok` only — acceptable, ingested, confirmed, accepted. Never decorative.

note.purpose: Status ink `warn` only — needs review, awaiting review, the unreviewed-AI badge, and the warning margin note.

plot.purpose: Status ink `bad` only — rescan required, quality check failed, errors, and the destructive button variant (coloured by the status rule, not a danger palette).

page-title.purpose: The ChartHead h1, once per screen, above the double rule.

dialog-title.purpose: Modal headings. 17px at the same weight carries the login heading and the no-access notice.

section-title.purpose: The Panel heading inside a sheet head — Archivo Narrow, uppercase, letterspaced.

body.purpose: Every row, cell, value and sentence. Descriptions cap at 68–70ch. lining-nums globally; tabular-nums on any figure in a column.

annotation.purpose: Field hints, margin notes, expanded band readouts, the qualifier line under a status count.

field-label.purpose: The .field-label primitive — every form label, table header cell, chart-head identification field and definition term.

fonts.note: Self-hosted, never CDN-linked: this system deploys on-premise inside hospital networks.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The whole vocabulary. Every Tailwind boxShadow step (sm, DEFAULT, md, lg, xl, 2xl, inner) is overridden to `none`, so a stray shadow utility renders flat. Depth is a border in one of two weights plus tonal stock layering.

shadows.name: modal-scrim
shadows.purpose: Not an elevation token — the single scrim behind the modal dialog, at exactly one site in the build.

motion.name: ease-chart
motion.purpose: The only authored easing: damped, single-axis, no overshoot. Applied to every colour transition and to the band-expand grid-row collapse.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: The only transition duration in the application. Used 11 times; no other duration exists.

motion.name: trace
motion.value: trace 1.4s cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1) infinite; @keyframes trace { 0% { transform: translateX(-110%) } 100% { transform: translateX(330%) } }
motion.purpose: The one authored motion in the application: a value being plotted. Used by the loading indicator and nowhere else.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation-duration: 0.001ms !important; transition-duration: 0.001ms !important; .trace { animation: none !important; inset: 0; width: 100% }
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every transition collapses to instant and the trace stops moving, leaving the whole track hatched — the honest still picture of a value that has not arrived.

layout.name: index-column
layout.value: 13.5rem (216px), md and up; a horizontal scrolling strip below md

layout.name: hairline
layout.value: --hair: 1px; 0.5px above 2dppx — a printed rule is one device pixel

layout.name: touch-target
layout.value: @media (pointer: coarse): 40px minimum control height, 1.15rem checkboxes and radios

textures.name: hatch
textures.value: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, rgb(var(--c-ink-2) / 0.2) 0, rgb(var(--c-ink-2) / 0.2) var(--hair), transparent var(--hair), transparent 6px)
textures.purpose: The one meaning-bearing texture: this region was never measured. Applied to an unmeasured status stamp, a band with no value, a band whose known value describes something unmeasured, and the stalled loading track. Never decoration; always paired with a text label. An empty result set is deliberately NOT hatched.

textures.name: chart-grid
textures.value: linear-gradient(to right, rgb(var(--c-rule) / 0.55) var(--hair), transparent var(--hair)), linear-gradient(to bottom, rgb(var(--c-rule) / 0.4) var(--hair), transparent var(--hair)); background-size: 8px 8px
textures.purpose: The printed measuring grid. Applied only to a region that actually plots a value against a scale — two sites in the build, both band tracks. Never page decoration.

textures.name: rule-double
textures.purpose: The double rule a printed form uses to close a section head. Present once per screen, under the ChartHead.

statusVocabulary.purpose: Single source of truth for how a status is worded and coloured; a screen never hand-writes a label for a status that has a canonical one.

fields.name: tone
fields.drives: the status ink only — border at 50%, wash at 7%, mark and text in full ink

fields.name: icon
fields.drives: the mark before the label, so the status survives greyscale and colour blindness (WCAG 1.4.1)

fields.name: qualifier
fields.drives: a short visible reason rendered beside the label — never hidden in a title, because no tooltip exists on the tablets this is used on

fields.name: unmeasured
fields.drives: the hatching — 15 statuses carry it, separating 'nothing was established' from 'nothing is there'

toneMap.neutral: ink-2 on paper-2 with a rule-2 border

narrative.overview:
This interface is the ward chart the hospital already runs on, made into an instrument. A figure is never stated as a bare number when a scale exists to read it against: the count sits in lining tabular numerals at the left of a ruled row, the band is plotted at its right, and the reference marks that give the band meaning open in place when the row is touched. It refuses the admin-console arrangement — a number floating in a soft rounded card with a coloured delta and nothing said about what it was measured against — and it refuses it structurally, not by taste: there are no cards in this system, the radius scale tops out at 2px, and every shadow utility resolves to `none`.

The material is chart stock, hairline rules and two inks. Density is deliberate and unapologetic — a records clerk works hundreds of rows a shift, so the body size is 13px, table rows are 6px tall in padding, and a screen fits what a screen fits. That density is never paid for by a finger: under `pointer: coarse` every control grows to a 40px minimum, because intake happens on tablets at the ward and the front desk.

The one idea the whole system is arranged around is the difference between *nothing was found* and *nothing was established*. A failed check, an unconfigured provider and a queued page all report an absence of knowledge; `none_detected` and `not_found` report a finding. The first group is drawn with a 45° graphite hatch — the chart convention for a region that was never measured — and the hatch appears nowhere else in the system, on nothing decorative, ever.
keyCharacteristics: Chart stock ground (#fbfaf6), hairline printed rules, two inks, no cards and no nesting
Every radius clamped to 2px; every box-shadow utility resolves to none
Colour only ever means status; chart blue is the single structural accent
Hatching is the one meaning-bearing texture and it means "never measured"
Archivo body, Archivo Narrow condensed caps for every pre-printed label; lining figures globally
One authored moment of motion, 150ms on a damped curve, collapsed to instant under reduced motion
Light and dark are the same eleven variables flipped by the OS; no dark: variant exists anywhere

rules.name: The Status-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Colour never means anything but status. `band`, `note` and `plot` appear only where a state is being reported; `chart` is the one structural accent and carries no verdict except `info`. Audit test: point at any coloured pixel and name the status it reports. If you cannot, it is a defect.

rules.name: The Enumerated Ink Rule
rules.body: The palette is eleven custom properties and adding a colour means adding one there. Anything that looks like a twelfth tone is a printed texture (a hatch, a tint of an existing ink at 7%/12%/22%), never a new hue.

rules.name: The Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: Colour is never the sole carrier of meaning. Every status ink ships with a drawn mark and a text label from `lib/status.ts`, so a stamp survives greyscale, any colour-vision profile, and a screen reader.

rules.name: The One Theme, Two Values Rule
rules.body: There are no `dark:` variants in this application — a grep returns zero. The eleven variables flip under `prefers-color-scheme` and every utility follows. Dark is the same chart read on a light box. No in-app theme toggle exists; clinical workstations are centrally configured.

rules.name: The Pre-Printed Label Rule
rules.body: Anything that names a box is set in Archivo Narrow, 11px, semibold, uppercase, 0.08em, in pencil grey. Anything written in the box is Archivo at 13px in writing ink. A label never borrows body type and a value never borrows label type.

rules.name: The Lining Figure Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: lining-nums is set on html because this application is almost entirely numbers, and every figure that sits in a column also carries tabular-nums so digits line up between rows.

rules.name: The Device-Pixel Rule
rules.body: A printed rule is one device pixel, not one CSS pixel. --hair is 1px, and 0.5px above 2dppx; the chart grid and the hatch are drawn from it.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Ink on paper does not float. If two things need separating, draw a rule or change the tone of the stock. Never reach for a shadow; the utility will not render one anyway.

rules.name: The 2px Ceiling
rules.body: No corner in this system exceeds 2px. There is no exception and no pill-shaped element.

rules.name: The Hatch-Means-Unmeasured Rule
rules.body: `.hatch` — 45° repeating pencil-grey lines at 20% on a 6px pitch — marks a region that was never measured, and nothing else. It is applied to a status stamp whose `unmeasured` flag is set, to a band with no value behind it, to a band whose known value describes something unmeasured, and to the stalled loading track. It is never decoration, and it is always paired with a text label so it is reinforcement rather than the signal. An empty result set is deliberately not hatched: the query ran and returned nothing, which is a finding.

rules.name: The Grid-Means-Scale Rule
rules.body: `.chart-grid` — an 8px printed measuring grid at --hair — appears only on a region that actually plots a value against a scale. Two sites in the build use it, both bands. It is never page decoration.

rules.name: The Single Moment Rule
rules.body: There is one authored motion in this application: `.trace`, the loading indicator. Everything else that moves is a 150ms ease-chart (cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1)) colour transition or the band-expand grid-row collapse — damped, single-axis, no overshoot, nothing self-animating. prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition to 0.001ms and stops the trace.

rules.name: The One Wording Rule
rules.body: A screen never hand-writes a label for a status that has a canonical one. `lib/status.ts` owns every label, tone, icon, qualifier and `unmeasured` flag, so a distinction that matters can only be got wrong in one place.

dos: Do plot a figure against the band it was measured against. If a scale exists, the number does not appear alone.
Do hatch anything whose status carries `unmeasured`, and pair the hatch with a text label — it is reinforcement, never the signal.
Do take every status label, tone, icon and qualifier from `lib/status.ts`, and render a qualifier visibly beside the label rather than in a `title`.
Do separate things with a rule (`rule` hairline, `rule-2` structural) or a change of stock tone (`paper` / `paper-2` / `paper-3`).
Do set anything that names a box in Archivo Narrow 11px semibold uppercase at 0.08em in pencil grey, and anything written in a box in Archivo 13px in writing ink.
Do give every figure in a column `tabular-nums`.
Do add new colour by adding a variable in `index.css` — both the light block and the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block — so the set stays enumerable.
Do keep the dense layout and let `pointer: coarse` pay for touch (40px minimum control height, 1.15rem checkboxes).
donts: Don't colour anything that is not a status. `band`, `note` and `plot` are verdict inks; `chart` is the one structural accent.
Don't write a `dark:` variant. There are none in the application; flip the custom properties instead and every utility follows.
Don't use `.hatch` as texture or `.chart-grid` as page decoration. The first means "never measured"; the second means "this region plots a value against a scale".
Don't reach for a shadow or an elevation. Every shadow utility resolves to `none`.
Don't exceed a 2px corner, and don't build a pill — `rounded-full` appears nowhere in the built application.
Don't nest a `.sheet` inside a `.sheet`, or introduce a card.
Don't hatch an empty result set. The query ran and returned nothing; that is a finding, and it gets the dashed empty field instead.
Don't shade an invented target band or draw a detent from a value the API did not supply.
Don't add a second moving part. `.trace` is the loading indicator and the only animation; everything else is 150ms `ease-chart`.
Don't put meaning behind a hover-only tooltip — intake and ward staff work on touch devices where no tooltip exists.
Don't invent a hospital name or logo. Identity surfaces carry the bordered `ScanLine` placeholder until the assets are supplied.
